<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par45 />{{GHGmargin-letter|45|g}}
The blending of the {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} with the ''Infin. constr.'' into a single grammatical form seems to be indicated by the firmly closed syllable, cf. {{GHGheb|text=לִשְׁכַּב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִנְפֹּל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=118|verse=13}}, with {{GHGterm|Dageš lene}} in the {{GHGheb|text=פ}}=''lin-pōl''; hence, also ''liq-ṭōl'', &c.; but {{GHGheb|text=בִּנְפֹל}} ''bin<sup>e</sup>phōl'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּנְפֹל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=3|verse=34}}. Exceptions {{GHGheb|text=לִצְבֹא}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=4|verse=23}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=8|verse=24|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִנְתוֹשׁ וְלִנְתוֹץ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=1|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=18|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=28|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִשְׁדוֹד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=47|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִטְבוֹחַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=11|verse=19}}, &c., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=לִבְדוֹק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=34|verse=10}}; according to some also {{GHGheb|text=לִסְבֹב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=4}} and {{GHGheb|text=לִכְבשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=28|verse=10}} (Baer {{GHGheb|text=לִכְבּשׁ}}); on the other hand {{GHGheb|text=בִּשְׁכֹּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=35|verse=22}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּזְכֹּר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=2}}. For the meaningless {{GHGheb|text=לְדַרְיוֹשׁ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=10|verse=16}} read {{GHGheb|text=לִדְרשׁ}}.<section end=par45 />
<section begin=par46 />{{GHGpar-heading|46|The Imperative}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|46|a}}
'''1.''' The ground-forms of the Imperative, {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}} (properly ''q<sup>e</sup>ṭŭl'', which is for an original ''qŭṭŭl''), and {{GHGheb|text=קְטַל}} (see below, c), the same in pronunciation as the forms of the Infin. constr. (§ 45), are also the basis for the formation of the Imperfect (§ 47).<ref>The ''Infin. absol.'', like the Greek Infin., is also sometimes used for the Imperative ({{GHGpar|113|bb}}). Cf. in general, Koch, ''Der semitische Inf.'' (Schaffhausen, 1874).</ref> They represent the ''second'' person, and have both fem. and plur. forms. The third person is supplied by the Imperfect in the Jussive ({{GHGpar|109|b}}); and even the second person must always be expressed by the Jussive, if it be used with a negative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אַל־תִּקְטֹל|translate=ne occidas}} (not {{GHGheb|text=אַל־קְטֹל}}). The passives have no Imperative, but it occurs in the reflexives, as Niphʿal and Hithpaʿēl.<ref>In {{GHGterm|Hophʿal}} an Imperative is found only twice ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer.|chapter=49|verse=8}}), and closely approximating in meaning to the reflexive.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|46|b}}
'''2.''' The Afformatives of the ''2nd sing. fem.'' and the ''2nd plur. masc.'' and {{GHGterm|fem.}} are identical in every case with those of the Imperfect ({{GHGpar|47|c}}). In the same way, the Imperative of the ''2nd sing. masc.'', in common with the Imperfect, admits of the lengthening by the {{GHGheb|text=־ָה|translate=paragogicum}} ({{GHGpar|48|i}}), as, on the other hand, there are certain shortened forms of this person analogous to the Jussive (§ 48. 5).

{{GHGmargin-letter|46|c}}
Rem. 1. Instead of the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטֹל}} (sometimes also {{GHGterm|plene}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שְׁמוֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=12|verse=13}}; before {{GHGterm|Maqqeph}} {{GHGheb|text=קְטָל־}} with {{GHGterm|Qameṣ ḥaṭuph}}), those verbs which have an ''a'' in the final syllable of the ''Imperf.'' (i.e. especially verbs middle ''ē'') make their Imperative of the form {{GHGheb|text=קְטַל}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=לְבַשֹׁ|translate=dress!}} (Perf. {{GHGheb|text=לָבַשׁ}} and {{GHGheb|text=לָבֵשׁ}}); {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכַב|translate=lie down!}} in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכָ֑ב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=5.6.9}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|46|d}}
2. The first syllable of the sing. fem. and plur. masc. are usually to be pronounced with {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ mobile}} (''qĭṭ<sup>e</sup>lî'', ''qĭṭ<sup>e</sup>lû'', and so {{GHGheb|text=שִׁפְכִי}}, &c., without {{GHGterm|Dageš lene}}, and even {{GHGheb|text=מִֽשְׁכוּ}} with {{GHGterm|Metheg}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=21}}; but cf. {{GHGheb|text=אִסְפִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=10|verse=17}}, and with the same phonetic combination {{GHGheb|text=חֶשְׂפִּי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=2}}; see analogous cases in {{GHGpar|93|m}}); less frequently we find an ''ŏ'' instead of the ''ĭ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מָלְכִי|translate=rule}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=9|verse=10}}; {{GHGheb|text=מָשְׁכוּ|translate=draw}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=20}}; {{GHGheb|text=חָרְבוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=12}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=חֳָרָ֑בִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=44|verse=27}}); on {{GHGheb|text=קָֽסֳמִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=28|verse=8}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}, {{GHGheb|text=צֳעָ֫קִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer.|chapter=22|verse=20}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=7}}), see {{GHGpar|10|h}}. This ''ŏ'' arises (see above, a) from a singular ground-form ''qŭṭŭl'', not from a retraction of the original ''ŭ'' of the second syllable. We must abandon the view that the forms with ''ĭ'' in the first syllable (cf. also<section end=par46 /><noinclude>
